cur:catacombs-vatican-gold-glass-lazarus.summary: On a deep blue ground, a tall Christ in tunic and pallium, his name partly legible in the inscription above, stretches out his rod towards the small swaddled figure of Lazarus in a temple-tomb approached by steps. It is one of the finest gold-glass images of the miracle.
facts: The inscription along the upper edge includes the name of Christ (…CRISTVS…).
Commons states that it is in the Vatican's Christian collections.

cur:monumental-mustair-feeding-5000.summary: Within a framed panel on the north wall, Christ, haloed, stands at the centre among a dense group of apostles, extending his hands over the food, while figures of the crowd recline in the lower part of the panel. Much of the painting is faded, but the composition of the miracle can still be read.
facts: The abbey of Saint John at Müstair, founded c. 780, preserves wall paintings of about 800 arranged in five registers: the life of David at the top, three rows on the youth, ministry and Passion of Christ, and below them scenes of Saint Andrew, joined on the west wall by a Last Judgment.
UNESCO, which inscribed the abbey in 1983, describes them as Switzerland's greatest series of figurative murals, painted around 800.
